messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT: Elevated AWS KMS latency/errors observed for us-west-2 starting ~2026-03-15T09:06:29Z. Multiple services reporting signing failures and startup aborts (ThrottlingException / 503). Auto-page to oncall.

raj: Got the page — I'm on it. Initial check: spikes in KMS API p99 latency to ~3s, increased 5xxs. Seeing fleet startup failures across redwood-runtime and key-manager sidecars.

maria: Confirming logs from runtime-prod-usw2: `error signing request: ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded` and `failed to fetch key metadata: 503 ServiceUnavailable`. Happening during instance boot and also async signing for request batches.

devin: Pulling metrics now — CloudWatch shows KMS API 5xx rate jumped at 09:05 and sustained for ~4m. Our KMS client retries are linear, not exponential. Might be making the thundering-herd worse during autoscale.

sylvia: Customer impact: short-lived failures to create new encryption keys and to sign tokens. Affected surfaces: instance startup (some nodes fail to join), token issuance (short retries), and batch ingestion where we sign payloads. Some customers seeing increased 500s on write operations. No full data loss reported.

raj: Triage plan (short):
1) Stop autoscaling that will spawn new instances in us-west-2 (prevent more startup failures).
2) Deploy immediate client-side mitigations: enable cached-key fallback for signing, increase retry backoff, and enable local in-memory key caching.
3) Contact AWS support + open health-check ticket.
4) Failover signing traffic for low-latency routes to us-east-1 KMS replicas where appropriate.

maria: I'm disabling the us-west-2 ASG autoscale policies now (policy id: asg-prod-runtime-usw2-42). Command:```bash
aws autoscaling suspend-processes --auto-scaling-group-name prod-runtime-usw2
```

devin: Rolling a small config change to runtime client in canary pool (10 instances) to enable aggressive client-side caching and exponential backoff. Config patch:```json
{"KMS_RETRY_STRATEGY": "exponential", "KMS_CACHE_TTL_MS": 300000}
```Applying to canary now.

carol-support: Noted customers who've opened tickets: ACME, FrontlineHealth. Support will message affected customers with the known issue note and estimated timelines.

aws-support-bot: Case opened: #1234567891. AWS investigating KMS control plane in us-west-2, root cause pending. Current status: degraded performance. Link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/12345 (internal).

raj: Canary looks promising: canary instances no longer show immediate signing failures after cache rollout. p95 latency for canary signing calls down from 2.7s -> 180ms. Starting staged rollout to 50% of runtime instances in us-west-2.

maria: Also applying a short-term change: switch token-issuer service to use service-account local keys for issuance if KMS calls fail >3 times. Adding feature flag: `kms_failover_local_keys=true`. Patch applied to token-issuer canary.

devin: Note: we also observed some KMS Throttling tied to one noisy job that was doing bulk re-encryption in the night window. We've paused that job. Job id: recrypt-20260315-7.

raj: Customer-facing status update drafted. sylvia please post to status.redwood.ai and send to support thread once I review. Short message: "We're experiencing elevated KMS API errors in us-west-2 causing intermittent token and request signing failures; mitigation in progress and we may see transient 5xxs for affected endpoints."

sylvia: Posted. Support DM sent to impacted customers.

maria: AWS just replied on the ticket: they see increased control plane latency due to adjacent service degradation and are applying mitigation on their side. ETA unknown. For safety we should plan for multi-hour window.

devin: Rollout update: 50% -> 100% of runtime instances in us-west-2 have the cache/backoff patch. No new startup signing failures observed in the last 10 minutes.

raj: Mitigations summary for next oncall:
- Autoscaling remains suspended for prod-runtime-usw2 until further notice.
- KMS client configured to exponential backoff + local caching.
- Token-issuer has local key fallback enabled via `kms_failover_local_keys` for 1h.
- Noisy re-encrypt job paused.
- AWS case #1234567891 open; policy/ops contact: aws-urgent@amazon.com.
- Customers notified; status page updated.

carol-support: Logging all affected customer IDs to the incident tracker (inc-1842006789) for post-incident follow-up.

aws-support-bot: Update: AWS applied throttling mitigation at 09:32 UTC, some control-plane metrics improving. Monitoring for stability.

raj: Handing off to night oncall (maria) at 09:40 UTC. If anything regresses: escalate to SRE lead + open a bridge. Handoff notes: we have stable canary->prod rollout, autoscale suspended, local fallback enabled, AWS case #1234567891 ongoing.

maria: Acknowledged handoff. I'll monitor CloudWatch and runtime logs for 2 hours, then reassess autoscale. If AWS restores normal KMS performance, we'll coordinate a controlled resume of autoscaling and disable the local failover flag.

devin: Postmortem TODOs (tracked):
- Add exponential backoff default to KMS client library.
- Implement jittered retry and improved circuit-breaker for KMS calls.
- Add pre-warm key cache during instance boot to avoid startup thundering herd.
- Revisit re-encrypt scheduling to reduce daytime risk.
- Customer RCA writeup and timeline.

sylvia: Filing incident with severity label: SEV-2 (partial customer impact). Will coordinate final customer comms after RCA.

incident-bot: Incident incident-1842006789 created and tagged SEV-2. Pager duty handoff recorded.

raj: Closing thread here; handoff complete. If anything else shows up, reopen or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
